note: Unvocalized أحضر has several very common readings: أَحْضَرَ 'brought', أَحْضِرْ 'bring!', and أَحْضُرُ 'I attend/am present'. The current gloss presents only the first family.
proposed_english: brought; brought in; supplied; bring!; I attend / I am present (depending on vocalization/context)
proposed_pos: perfect-past verb / imperative verb / first-person imperfect verb

note: شخصية also functions adjectivally as the feminine form 'personal', in addition to the nouns personality/character.
proposed_english: personality; character; personal (feminine, depending on use)

note: رياضي commonly means not only athletic/sporting but also an athlete/sportsman and a mathematician, depending on context.
مؤكدا represents an accusative participial/adverbial form (مؤكِّدًا / مؤكَّدًا), not a noun. The POS and learner gloss should reflect confirming/emphasizing vs confirmed/certain readings.
proposed_english: confirming; emphasizing; confirmed; certain; definitely (depending on vocalization/context)
proposed_pos: active/passive participle / adjective used adverbially or circumstantially

note: حالي can also be حال + possessive suffix ي, meaning 'my condition/state', a common surface reading omitted by the adjective-only entry.
proposed_english: current; present; my condition; my state (depending on structure)

note: سوى is traditionally an exceptive noun (اسم استثناء) meaning 'except/other than', not an exceptive particle.
أشهر is both the plural 'months' (أَشْهُر) and the elative 'more/most famous' (أَشْهَر), a very common reading omitted by the entry.
proposed_english: months; more famous; most famous (depending on vocalization/use)

note: ملك is a major unvocalized homograph: مَلِك 'king', مَلَك 'angel', مِلْك 'property/possession', and مَلَكَ 'owned/possessed'. Teaching only 'angel' is materially incomplete.
proposed_english: king; angel; property; possession; owned; possessed (depending on vocalization/use)

note: صعب is very commonly the adjective صَعْب 'difficult/hard', not only the perfect verb 'was difficult/became hard'.
proposed_english: difficult; hard; was difficult; became hard (depending on vocalization/use)
